neighbours.label: the position just before a term for part of the self in psychological or spiritual discussion (' the' before ego / body / mind / super-ego), where the model expects 'ego'-like words; the same 'between X and the Y' frames about everyday objects stay low
fire: Psychoanalysts speak of a struggle between the id and the ego in every person.
The yogi teaches that we must stop identifying with the body to find freedom.
In Freud's model, guilt comes from the superego judging the ego.
Meditation slowly loosens our attachment to the mind and its stories.
The therapist explained how the ego defends itself against anxiety.
Buddhist teachers say suffering comes from clinging to the self.
According to the Upanishads, the true self is not the body but pure awareness.
Freud believed the conscious mind is only a small part of the psyche.
quiet: The children ran back and forth between the house and the barn all day.
The mechanic teaches that we must stop ignoring the brakes to stay safe.
In the old model, the gears turn the shaft and the shaft turns the wheel.
Rust slowly loosens the grip of the bolts on the old engine.
The guide explained how the castle defended itself against attack.
Climbing teachers say falls come from clinging to the rock too tightly.
According to the manual, the main switch is not on the box but on the wall.
The engineer believed the cooling fan was only a small part of the problem.
